idiom_name: try/catch or Promise.allSettled partial results, bounded by AbortSignal.timeout
implementation_notes: The idiom is error handling plus the aggregate combinators: try/catch (or .catch) around the primary call, and Promise.allSettled when a fan-out should keep whatever succeeded - each outcome carries status: "fulfilled" or "rejected", which is exactly "keep serving the parts that still work". What replaces the classic degraded-mode object is the shape of the returned payload: a partial list plus an explicit degraded/partial flag, with AbortSignal.timeout(ms) bounding the slow dependency so the fallback runs before the caller gives up. Node adds a process-level hazard: an unconsumed promise rejection terminates the process, so every degraded branch must consume its rejection.
pitfalls: Promise.all rejects on the first failure and discards the successes - the opposite of degradation; use allSettled (or any) when partial results are acceptable.
An unhandled rejection is fatal in current Node, so a degraded branch that ignores its rejection crashes the process it was meant to protect.
Cached substitutes need a TTL or max-age stamp: stale-while-revalidate can serve stale data forever while the refresh keeps failing, and clients treat it as fresh.
